questions.q: A column's mean is 129.8 but its median is 58.5. What does this most likely suggest?
options: The column has missing values
The data is sorted incorrectly
The column is stored as text
A few very large values are pulling the mean upward
questions.explain: The median is robust to extreme values while the mean is not. A large gap between them often signals outliers.

questions.q: In the IQR rule, which values are flagged as outliers?
options: Values below Q1 - 1.5 x IQR or above Q3 + 1.5 x IQR
Values more than 3 rows from the median
Values below the 25th percentile
The highest and lowest value in every column
questions.explain: The fences sit 1.5 IQRs beyond the first and third quartiles; anything outside them is flagged.

questions.q: In the lesson's 12-order example, the 940 order has a z-score of only about 3.17 even though it is clearly extreme. Why?
options: z-scores only work on integers
pandas computes z-scores incorrectly
The extreme value itself inflates the standard deviation used to measure it, which limits z-scores in small samples
940 is not really an outlier
questions.explain: The outlier increases both the mean and the standard deviation, so its own z-score is compressed. The IQR rule, based on quartiles, is less affected.

questions.q: You find that an order amount of 940 is a genuine sale to a corporate customer. What is the best treatment?
options: Delete the row because it is above the fence
Keep it, and consider robust statistics or reporting results with and without it
Replace it with the mean
Convert the whole column to category
questions.explain: A real value is real information. Deleting it because it is extreme would misrepresent the data; report sensitivity instead.

questions.q: Which approach caps extreme values while keeping the analysis transparent?
options: df.dropna() on the amount column
Overwrite amount with clip() and discard the original values
Create a capped column with clip(lower=low, upper=high) and an is_outlier flag, keeping the original amount
df.drop_duplicates(subset=["amount"])
questions.explain: clip pulls values to the fences. Keeping the original column and a flag documents exactly what was changed.
